page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.2xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it features 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The instance is configured with 64.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It operates on the KVM hypervisor, lacks local storage, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals that the CPU performance of the ecs.se1ne.2xlarge is generally modest. Single-core and multi-core stress-ng tests, alongside Geekbench single-core and multi-core evaluations, place the instance in the weak to poor categories, representing the bottom 10% to 25% of tested hardware. Memory bandwidth read performance is also weak, though large block write performance reaches average levels. Passmark CPU and extended instruction tests score in the average range, but database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput remain in the bottom 25%. LLM inference with a small 135M model achieves average speeds, but performance drops to poor with a medium 7B model.

The primary tradeoff of this instance is its high memory capacity paired with relatively low compute and memory bandwidth performance. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.se1ne.2xlarge is suited for memory-bound workloads that do not require intensive CPU processing or high-speed local storage. Appropriate workloads include caching layers, lightweight database operations, and memory-intensive applications with moderate throughput requirements.
